title: Mortgagee Rights under the NFIP General Property Form and RCBAP Flood Policies (Write Your Own)
content:
**Mortgage-required policies.** A policy under the NFIP General Property Form and RCBAP Flood Policies (Write Your Own) is mortgage-required when a federally regulated lender requires flood coverage as a condition of a loan secured by the building in a Special Flood Hazard Area; the first mortgagee and loan number are shown on the policy.

**Changing the mortgagee.** A mortgagee change endorsement replaces the mortgagee of record and the loan number on the date it is recorded, and a mortgagee can be removed only with that mortgagee's written release or a payoff letter.

**Notice and protection.** When a mortgage-required policy is cancelled or is not renewed, Tidemark sends written notice to the mortgagee of record on the date the cancellation is processed or the grace period ends; the policy then continues for the benefit of the mortgagee only for the tier's mortgagee protection period in calendar days after that notice.

**Payees.** Building claim payments are issued jointly to the insured and the mortgagee of record when the tier names the mortgagee on building payments; contents, ICC and loss-avoidance payments go to the insured alone.

| Payment | Payee |
|---|---|
| Building claim payment | the insured and the mortgagee of record |
| Contents claim payment | the insured alone |
| ICC payment | the insured alone |
| Loss-avoidance payment | the insured alone |

**Illustration (hypothetical).** A mortgage-required policy cancelled and processed on 5 March: written notice goes to the mortgagee of record that day, and the policy protects only the mortgagee for the 30 days that follow under the cancellation terms sheet.
